title: KV cache key-collision and cross-tenant prefix leakage — follow-up & remediation plan
creator: Ava Patel
description: This ticket tracks follow-ups for the KV cache key-collision incident on 2026-03-09 that caused cross-tenant prefix leakage and incorrect generation responses for a subset of requests. The scope includes short-term mitigations, rollout of an LRU indexing fix, audit tooling to detect key-space collisions, and post-release validation and alerts.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 at ~03:12 UTC a regression in prefix canonicalization introduced non-unique cache keys for a specific set of model prefixes (multi-segment prefixes with non-ASCII whitespace). This produced cache hits across tenant boundaries for ~1.3% of requests to the affected models, leading to incorrect token generation or stale completions. The control plane routing prevented customer exfiltration but served incorrect outputs for affected calls. No PII was identified in leaked cache entries. Incident duration: ~5h from detection to final mitigation.
timeline: 2026-03-09 03:10 UTC - deploy of runtime-1.21.5 containing canonicalization change; 2026-03-09 03:40 UTC - first spike in mismatch alerts (automated tests passed); 2026-03-09 04:05 UTC - error rate and client complaints begin; 2026-03-09 06:00 UTC - hotfix revert of canonicalization change rolled out to 30% then 100%; 2026-03-09 07:30 UTC - prefix audit job run and scope estimated; 2026-03-09 08:45 UTC - temporary stricter cache partitioning enabled (per-tenant salt); 2026-03-09 09:30 UTC - monitoring confirmed reduction in cross-tenant hits; 2026-03-09 10:10 UTC - incident declared resolved; 2026-03-10 onward - follow-up engineering triage and this action plan created.
root_cause: A change to prefix canonicalization (trim/normalize function) removed a normalization step for certain whitespace sequences and unicode normalization (NFKC) for multi-segment prefixes. The canonicalizer produced identical keys for different logical prefixes in edge cases. The hash function and key namespace lacked a per-tenant salt, so identical canonicalized bytes across tenants mapped to the same cache slots. The combination of canonicalization regression + no tenant salt = cross-tenant cache collision (semantically a poisoning bug).
mitigations: Short-term: reverted the canonicalization change (hotfix) and enabled per-tenant cache salt to stop cross-tenant collisions. Enabled an emergency alert for >0.05% cross-tenant cache hits and a dashboard widget showing cache hit origin by tenant. Medium-term: deploy a non-destructive prefix-audit job to scan key-space for similarities and run against a 7-day sliding window. Long-term: redesign key construction to include explicit tenant namespace + versioned key prefix and add stronger invariants in unit/integration tests.
action_items: A1: Implement tenant-salted key schema and migration plan. Owner: Rafael Ortega. ETA: 2026-03-28. Ticket: ENG-9071.
A2: Restore canonicalization with proper unicode normalization (NFKC) and a comprehensive test matrix for whitespace/unicode. Owner: Marta Kim. ETA: 2026-03-21. PR: runtime#2056.
A3: Add a pre-commit integration test that fuzzes prefix inputs and asserts key-uniqueness across tenant IDs. Owner: Jonah Li. ETA: 2026-03-18. Test harness: infra-tests/prefix-fuzz.
A4: Create an offline audit job that detects near-collisions (Levenshtein threshold) and surfaces candidate keys daily. Owner: Priya Desai. ETA: 2026-03-22. Dashboard: kv-collision-audit.
A5: Expand SLO/alerting to include cross-tenant hit rate and anomalous hit provenance. Owner: Observability Team (lead: Noor Singh). ETA: 2026-03-17. Grafana alerts added.
A6: Run a security review and external audit for cache isolation guarantees and publish findings to Security Review board. Owner: Security (lead: Damian Green). ETA: 2026-03-30.
A7: Post-release canary validation: synthetic prefixes + tenants exercised across replicas for 72 hours after runtime-1.22 rollout. Owner: Release Eng. ETA: coincide with runtime-1.22 rollout.

A8: Customer communication: send targeted incident notices to impacted customers and offer technical write-ups and follow-ups. Owner: Customer Success (lead: Lina Morales). ETA: 2026-03-16. Template: confluence/incident-templates/kv-leak
rollback_plan: If tenant-salted key schema causes regressions during rollout, revert to the emergency per-tenant salt and disable the new indexing; promote a quick patch to canonicalization (A2) as the fallback. Rollback owners: Rafael Ortega (runtime) + SRE on-call.
postmortem_notes:
- No evidence of exfiltration beyond cached tokens; control plane logs show no cross-tenant storage reads outside the cache layer.
- Concurrency tests did not cover unicode/whitespace edge cases — gap added to test matrix.
- The per-tenant salt emergency toggle was effective but is not a long-term fix because it complicates cache migration and increases memory usage slightly.
- Need clearer ownership for key schema and invariants (storage + runtime teams).
risks: Migration of cache keys to tenant-salted schema will increase cache miss rate during rollout and may temporarily increase tail latency. The audit/fuzz jobs may produce false positives that require triage. Security review may identify larger isolation concerns that impact release timing.
communication_plan: Draft sent to CS + SOC for review. Public status page note to be posted after release confirmation. Technical incident report and PR summary to be included in the monthly infra review. Security will coordinate customer-facing language for regulated customers.
follow_up_meeting: Scheduled: 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC. Attendees: ENG runtime, SRE, Security, Observability, Product. Agenda: review A1-A5 progress, decide rollback/testing gating for runtime-1.22, finalize customer comms.
notes: Assign ENG-9071 for migration work and ENG-9072 for canary validation tasks. Keep this ticket open until runtime-1.22 has run 72-hour canary without regressions.
